messages:
omar: FYI after the 175-rewrite deploy we're seeing higher KV cache churn and a bunch of GPU OOMs on staging. Root cause hypothesis: eviction/TTL behavior + new kernel selection memory accounting mismatch.

jin: Can you post the hit-rate numbers and memory graphs?

omar: Hit-rate summary (prefix cache, per-model aggregate): before deploy = 78% avg, after = 52% avg. GPU KV resident bytes dropped ~30% while host pinned went up 2.4x. LRU churn metric (evictions/sec) increased from 120 -> 370.

sara: Oof. Which change touched caching? kernel selection or batching?

omar: A couple of things landed in the same window: (1) kernel-selector now prefers fused attention on sequence>2048 which changed memory layout, (2) batching heuristics changed pad-trimming which increases unique cache key variation, (3) a small accounting bug in the allocator that double-counted temp host buffers for certain kernels.

mike: That double-count sounds like an allocator bug that would reduce perceived free memory and trigger more aggressive evictions. Can we reproduce with a controlled job?

omar: Yes — I reproduced on staging with a synthetic trace. Patch disabled fused-kernel preference and hit-rate recovered to ~75%. With accounting fix + targeted TTL change we get back to ~80%.

elaine: What TTL/warmup config did you try?

omar: Experiment config snapshot:
```json
{
  "kv": {
    "gpu_resident_limit_mb": "40960",
    "cpu_resident_limit_mb": "16384",
    "ttl_seconds": 120,
    "soft_limit_ratio": 0.85,
    "eviction_policy": "lru",
    "key_normalization": "strip_user_id, normalize_prompt_whitespace"
  }
}
```
- Baseline had ttl 300. Lowering to 120 reduced fragmentation because entries expired earlier and allowed coalescing.
- Added soft_limit_ratio so we trigger background GC before hard OOM.

jin: Did you try segmented LRU (by prefix length bucket)? That can help keep short prefixes hot.

omar: Yup. Segmented LRU by prefix token count (0-32,33-128,129+) helped hit-rate for common short prompts (+6%) and reduced eviction oscillation.

sara: How are you keying prefixes now? We've seen key skews when user ids or ephemeral salts are in key.

omar: We normalized keys (strip user id + canonicalize whitespace + truncate session meta). That recovered several previously low-hit keys. Still seeing some variation from trimming heuristics in batching.

mike: Warmup strategies? Pre-warming top-k prefixes on model load? Async restore from disk?

omar: Implemented async prefetch for top-200 prefixes per route after model load; also background restore of evicted hot items from SSD if evicted < 60s ago. That cut cold-start miss tail by ~45ms median.

elaine: Any perf regressions from kernel changes besides memory accounting? latency spikes?

omar: Latency p50 improved slightly with fused kernels for long sequences, but p99 saw regressions due to GC pauses triggered by eviction storms. With soft limits + segmented LRU we eliminated most p99 spikes.

jin: Ops question — do we need different GPU/CPU resident ratios per model? Some small models waste GPU residency.

omar: Yes, per-model sizing helps. We added a heuristic: small models get CPU-first residency with a higher TTL on CPU; large decoder models get GPU-priority. That reduced cross-model fragmentation.

mike: Can we add a safety net: abort/queue requests when eviction rate > threshold to avoid cascading OOM?

omar: Proposed flow: if evictions/sec > 500 AND free_gpu_mb < 5% -> request throttling for non-critical routes + escalate alert. Simple circuit-breaker implemented in staging.

elaine: Any follow-ups I should take on for the rollout?

omar: Action items: 1) merge allocator accounting fix (PR #4821), 2) enable soft_limit_ratio default 0.85, 3) deploy segmented LRU opt-in flag for two weeks, 4) add per-model resident config and default heuristics, 5) add circuit-breaker metric-based throttle.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled for 1752050000 -> will monitor kv_evictions, gpu_free_mb, prefix_hit_rate.

jin: I'll own the canary dashboard alerts and add regression test with synthetic trace.

sara: I'll update the docs for keying rules and warmup recommendations.

mike: I'll review PR #4821 now. :thumbsup:

omar: Thanks all — aiming to get canary out today and roll to prod tomorrow if stable.
